runways.note: OSM way 219359696 (3,962 m, full pavement) with displaced-threshold segment way 1064563478; ours sit at the 16R displaced landing threshold (ourairports lists 16R displaced 279 ft). ends[0]=16R end ok.

Ours = 16L displaced threshold (OSM way 186842426 / 510285760 split at -33.95166). OurAirports lists the pavement start 242 m north of that (-33.94960) because 16L has a 758 ft displaced threshold; ours is the correct landing threshold.
OSM way 219847158 (07/25). ourairports 25 end has 324 ft displaced threshold; ours matches OSM 25 end.

Ours is about 950 m too far south-east: it was centred on the ERSA aerodrome reference point (335327S 1504306E), which is NOT the runway centre. Correct runway centre is about [150.7130,-33.8834] (OSM way 968004296 3,700 m 05/23, and midpoint of the ERSA ILS localiser antennas LOC IWS 335335.8S 1504134.0E and LOC IWN 335225.0S 1504359.5E, which sit ~310 m beyond each end; ourairports airport coordinate -33.883461,150.712981 agrees). Use ends[0]=[150.69573,-33.89185] (05 threshold), ends[1]=[150.73025,-33.87504] (23 threshold). Runway 3,700 m x 45 m, bearing 047 mag (about 060 true). ERSA: https://www.airservicesaustralia.com/aip/current/ersa/FAC_YSWS_03SEP2026.pdf. OSM way is tagged source=ESRI (imagery trace), so thresholds are good to roughly 20-30 m, and cross-checked against the ILS data.

Future second runway: only the offset is wrong because it inherits the 950 m error of the first runway. Official: second parallel runway (05R/23L) on the southern side of the airport site, about 1,900 m from the first, needed when demand nears 37 million passengers a year (about 2050s, not before 2040). Exact longitudinal stagger and thresholds are NOT published in anything I could read, so keep cert as concept; Suggested placement if kept as a concept: first runway (corrected) shifted 1.9 km towards the south-east (bearing 60+90 true): 05R threshold [150.70613, -33.90667], 23L threshold [150.74065, -33.88986]. Placement accuracy: offset about +/-100 m, along-runway stagger unknown (could be several hundred m), so keep cert concept.

flightPaths.departs: Jets take off northwards and turn at 800 ft or 1,500 ft depending on track; LTOP mode 9 sends 34L departures 'over the north and north-west' (turn left/west of north), non-jets turn very early to the south-west. Roughly straight north then left towards the north-west; no right turns published for 34L.
flightPaths.arrives: Not used for arrivals in north flow? Arrivals land 34L from the SOUTH over Botany Bay (over-water, straight final). Heavy long-haul jets prefer 34L/16R (longest runway).

flightPaths.departs: Most departures turn east or north-east after take-off (right turn, away from the inner west); non-jets go straight ahead over Newtown/Glebe/Pyrmont at 2,500-4,000 ft.
flightPaths.arrives: Arrivals from the south over Botany Bay (straight final).

flightPaths.departs: Straight out over Botany Bay then a U-turn over water at about 6,000 ft; from 30 Nov 2023 all follow one consistent path and turn over water at one location before crossing the Royal National Park coast at 10,000 ft or more. Curfew (11pm-6am): all departures use 16R. Option of left turn through Botany Bay Heads discussed in LTOP but not confirmed.
flightPaths.arrives: Arrivals on 16R come from the north on a straight final over Lilyfield/Leichhardt/Stanmore (inner west).

flightPaths.departs: Jet departures track through the bay between Kurnell and La Perouse; from 30 Nov 2023 closer to the centre of Botany Bay (roughly straight south, slight right/left drift only). Non-jets turn left immediately after take-off.
flightPaths.arrives: Arrivals from the north on a straight final over Rozelle/Annandale/Camperdown/Newtown.

flightPaths.departs: Not published in the sources I could read in detail. Mode 14A has arrivals from the west on 07; LTOP says departure tracks east off 07 needed further development (kept off the reciprocal of the 25 arrival track), i.e. over Botany Bay/the coast.
flightPaths.arrives: Arrivals on 07 come straight in from the west over the inner west/Canterbury-Bankstown corridor (14A: arrivals from the west on 07).

flightPaths.departs: Jets hold runway track to 1,500 ft then take the heading ATC assigns (modes: departures to the north-west, west and south-west from 25). Both left and right turns used.
flightPaths.arrives: Arrivals from the east over Botany Bay/Brighton-le-Sands (LTOP mode 5, straight final).

flightPaths.departs: Curfew 11pm-6am (departures 16R, arrivals 34L). Noise-sharing runway modes (LTOP) are used when wind and traffic allow; over-water modes preferred. New Sydney airspace from 9 July 2026 to fit WSI; I found no published change to YSSY runway-end turn directions in the pages I could read.

Day (runway 05 into the north-east): left turns after take-off are delayed (restricted Orchard Hills defence area) and designed to track as far west of St Clair as possible; westbound departures stay north of the Great Western Highway; eastbound departures climb west/south-west then turn east. Map draws straight 22 km departures (depKm 22): wrong shape (real tracks turn after the first ~km), no numeric turn angles published.
flightPaths.arrives: Arrivals from the south-west; turns onto final are designed to avoid low overflight of Silverdale, so final is straight only for the last ~10-15 km.

flightPaths.departs: Day (runway 23 into the south-west): RIGHT turns for jets delayed to avoid Silverdale; departures to the north cross the Great Western Highway at a low-density area; southbound turns gain height over non-residential land. Night RRO: take off on 23 to the south-west, turn as early as possible.
flightPaths.arrives: Arrivals from the north-east (Day) straight in over the north-west; night arrivals use 05 from the south-west, turning onto final south-west of The Oaks / south of Silverdale (~20 km out).

aerodrome way icao=YSWS, about 6.8 km2, bbox 150.685-150.739 / -33.906 to -33.870. Note the OSM runway way is correct but the map's runway coordinates are not (see runways).
